children: Tighter U.S. chip controls are unlikely to disrupt Malaysia's committed data-center projects but could delay future phases of expansion, particularly those involving Chinese-linked customers, MBSB Research's Ming San Soong says in a note. Projects backed by established U.S. hyperscalers should remain largely intact, supporting contractors' order books over the next 12 months, the analyst says. However, stricter U.S. chip-export rules could raise the bar for future developments, she adds. Sunway Construction has the biggest data-center exposure, while Gamuda, IJM and Kerjaya Prospek have more diversified portfolios, Soong notes. MBSB maintains a positive rating on the Malaysian construction sector, with Gamuda, Sunway Construction and IJM as its top picks. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
